newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 707c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 707c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose seven cents to 707 cents a kg clean on Wednesday at sales in Sydney, Wool International said, adding that some category indicator movements could be partly attributed to a centre effect.
Merino fleece was dearer, with 19/20 microns up two percent, 21m up 1.5 percent, 22/23m up one percent and 24/25/26 up 0.5 percent.
Merino skirtings of 19m were generally unchanged with 20/21/22m slightly dearer.
Crossbreds were cheaper on a limited offering, with 27m slightly cheaper, 28m 0.5 percent cheaper, 29/31 up to one percent cheaper and 30m three percent cheaper.
In cardings, locks and crutchings were one percent cheaper.
WI said Japanese interests were principal buyers with good support from most sectors of the trade.
Of the 10,680 bales offered, 3.6 percent were passed in.
Sales continue on Thursday in Sydney and Fremantle with about 28,000 bales to be offered.
